knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A cleaner does not open or sort potentially infectious or uncertain items. The bag is closed, labelled as directed, placed in the designated holding area, and the supervisor is told; the facility decides the stream.

A body-fluid spill is restricted and escalated to the trained spill response person and the supervisor. A cleaner only cleans spills they are trained and authorised for, so wiping it up is not correct.
A cleaner does not handle sharps by hand. They keep others away and call the designated sharps response person, and never push the needle into a bin or under furniture.

practicalCriteria: Given a damp bag of linen where the moisture cannot be identified, the learner does not open it, closes and labels it as directed, places it in the holding area, and tells the supervisor.
Given an unidentified spill on a corridor floor, the learner restricts access and calls the trained spill response person and the supervisor, without wiping the spill.
Given a loose needle on a treatment room floor, the learner does not touch it, keeps others away, and calls the sharps response person.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% pass mark, which for three checks means all three correct. Practical competence needs facility-observed assessment against the practical criteria, and a knowledge pass does not count as practical competence.
evidenceRequired: Record of the holding-area placement with location, time and person told
Observation note of the spill escalation
Observation note of the sharps response
stopWorkCriteria: Learner opens or sorts an uncertain bag of linen or waste
Learner wipes or cleans a body-fluid or unknown spill without training and authorisation
Learner picks up a sharp by hand or pushes it into a bin
